raw:
{
  "items": [
    {
      "category": "domain_extent",
      "entity": "Square plate side length",
      "issue": "vague",
      "description": "Sec. 4.1 gives L = 1 m, and Sec. 4.1.1 specifies a square, but the text does not explicitly relate its side length to L; the dimension annotations in Fig. 6a are unavailable.",
      "readings": [
        "Square side equals L.",
        "Square side equals 2L, with L denoting a half-side dimension."
      ],
      "effect": "layout"
    },
    {
      "category": "support_location_extent",
      "entity": "Fixed boundary Gamma_u",
      "issue": "figure_only",
      "description": "Sec. 4.1.1 locates the fixed boundary through Fig. 6a. Its position, number of segments, and extent are not described. Both displacement components are explicitly fixed.",
      "readings": [
        "Fix the entire left edge.",
        "Fix two left-edge patches, each covering one tenth of the side, at the upper and lower corners.",
        "Fix the entire bottom edge."
      ],
      "effect": "layout"
    },
    {
      "category": "load_position",
      "entity": "Traction boundary Gamma_t",
      "issue": "figure_only",
      "description": "Sec. 4.1.1 calls the loading asymmetric but relies on Fig. 6a for the loaded edge, offsets, and number of loaded segments.",
      "readings": [
        "One right-edge patch centered at one quarter of the plate height.",
        "One top-edge patch centered at three quarters of the plate width.",
        "Two simultaneously loaded right-edge patches centered at one quarter and one half of the plate height."
      ],
      "effect": "layout"
    },
    {
      "category": "load_extent_distribution",
      "entity": "Length of the traction application region",
      "issue": "figure_only",
      "description": "Sec. 4.1 specifies traction magnitude but gives no length or endpoints for Gamma_t in Fig. 6a. Consequently, the resultant force is also undetermined.",
      "readings": [
        "Apply the stated traction uniformly over a segment of length 0.05 times the square side.",
        "Apply the stated traction uniformly over a segment of length 0.10 times the square side.",
        "Apply the stated traction uniformly over an entire edge."
      ],
      "effect": "layout"
    },
    {
      "category": "load_direction",
      "entity": "Traction vector on Gamma_t",
      "issue": "figure_only",
      "description": "Sec. 4.1 gives only the vector magnitude; neither Sec. 4.1.1 nor the Fig. 6 caption supplies its direction.",
      "readings": [
        "Vertically downward.",
        "Horizontally leftward.",
        "Diagonally downward and leftward at 45 degrees."
      ],
      "effect": "layout"
    },
    {
      "category": "passive_region",
      "entity": "Finite solid attachment pads at supports and loads",
      "issue": "missing",
      "description": "Sec. 4.1 does not describe finite passive solid pads. The auxiliary-domain boundary condition alone does not specify whether any adjacent structured-grid cells must remain solid.",
      "readings": [
        "No finite passive cells; enforce only the stated boundary conditions.",
        "Keep a one-cell-thick solid band adjoining the loaded boundary.",
        "Keep one-cell-thick solid bands adjoining both loaded and fixed boundaries."
      ],
      "effect": "layout"
    },
    {
      "category": "filter_or_solver_setting",
      "entity": "Beta values in the Sec. 4.1.1 sweep",
      "issue": "vague",
      "description": "Sec. 4.1.1 specifies the interval from beta = 2 to beta = 8, but not the discrete values tested; Fig. 7 supplies no textual list.",
      "readings": [
        "Separate runs at beta = 2, 4, 6, 8.",
        "Separate runs at beta = 2, 5, 8.",
        "Separate runs at every integer beta from 2 through 8."
      ],
      "effect": "layout"
    },
    {
      "category": "filter_or_solver_setting",
      "entity": "Numerical initial fields phi_0 and phi_-1",
      "issue": "missing",
      "description": "Sec. 4.1 specifies fully filled initial geometries, but not the positive level-set values or profiles representing them. Identical geometry does not uniquely determine either numerical field or their difference.",
      "readings": [
        "Set both fields to 1 throughout the interior.",
        "Set both fields to 0.5 throughout the interior.",
        "Set phi_0 to 1 and phi_-1 to 0.5 throughout the interior."
      ],
      "effect": "layout"
    },
    {
      "category": "filter_or_solver_setting",
      "entity": "Enforcement of the level-set range",
      "issue": "missing",
      "description": "Sec. 2.1 restricts phi to [-1,1], but Sec. 3 does not explain how that restriction is enforced after the wave update.",
      "readings": [
        "Clip each updated nodal value to [-1,1].",
        "Rescale the updated interior field by max(1, its maximum absolute value), then restore prescribed boundary values.",
        "Enforce the bounds through a constrained update solve."
      ],
      "effect": "layout"
    },
    {
      "category": "filter_or_solver_setting",
      "entity": "Level-set Dirichlet value on auxiliary boundary G_t",
      "issue": "conflicting",
      "description": "Secs. 2.2 and 3 and the strong wave problem in Appendix A.1 prescribe phi = 1, whereas the weak wave formulation in Appendix A.1 prescribes phi_(v+1) = 0.",
      "readings": [
        "Prescribe phi = 1.",
        "Prescribe phi = 0."
      ],
      "effect": "layout"
    },
    {
      "category": "filter_or_solver_setting",
      "entity": "Intermediate material and stiffness sensitivity",
      "issue": "conflicting",
      "description": "Eq. (23) makes Theta smooth, but Sec. 4.1 invokes binary identities to obtain Eq. (41). For smooth Theta and q = 3, the derivative of Eq. (40) contains Theta squared, whereas Eq. (41) contains Theta.",
      "readings": [
        "Use smooth Theta in volume and cubic stiffness interpolation, with the linear-in-Theta sensitivity printed in Eq. (41).",
        "Use smooth Theta in volume and cubic stiffness interpolation, with the exact sensitivity 3(1-e)Theta squared.",
        "Use binary Theta in volume and stiffness, and the binary sensitivity expression in Eq. (41)."
      ],
      "effect": "layout"
    },
    {
      "category": "filter_or_solver_setting",
      "entity": "Initial augmented-Lagrangian multiplier",
      "issue": "missing",
      "description": "Sec. 4.1 supplies a multiplier update rule but no initial multiplier. Here J_full denotes the initial filled-domain compliance.",
      "readings": [
        "Initialize the multiplier to zero.",
        "Initialize the multiplier to 0.1 J_full.",
        "Initialize the multiplier to J_full."
      ],
      "effect": "layout"
    },
    {
      "category": "filter_or_solver_setting",
      "entity": "Augmented-Lagrangian penalty schedule",
      "issue": "missing",
      "description": "Following Eq. (42), r increases each iteration until r_max, but its initial value, growth rule, and cap are absent. Here J_full denotes the initial filled-domain compliance.",
      "readings": [
        "Start r at J_full and multiply by 1.1 each iteration, capped at 1000 J_full.",
        "Start r at 0.1 J_full and multiply by 2 each iteration, capped at 10000 J_full."
      ],
      "effect": "layout"
    },
    {
      "category": "filter_or_solver_setting",
      "entity": "Sensitivity normalization C_v",
      "issue": "vague",
      "description": "Eq. (44) places an L2(D) magnitude inside another domain integral without clarifying whether it denotes a global norm or a pointwise magnitude. Let a(x) be the local stiffness-sensitivity density.",
      "readings": [
        "Interpret the inner quantity as a global L2 norm, giving C_v = ||a||_L2 because c_f = 1.",
        "Interpret it as pointwise absolute magnitude, giving C_v = integral_D |a(x)| dx / V_0."
      ],
      "effect": "layout"
    },
    {
      "category": "filter_or_solver_setting",
      "entity": "Previous-step term in the wave update",
      "issue": "conflicting",
      "description": "Eq. (32), the subsequent weak and matrix forms, and Appendix A.1 use minus phi_(v-1). Eq. (34) instead prints minus phi_v, which also produces a different update when m = k = 0.",
      "readings": [
        "Use the history term 2 phi_v - phi_(v-1).",
        "Follow Eq. (34) literally and use 2 phi_v - phi_v."
      ],
      "effect": "layout"
    },
    {
      "category": "filter_or_solver_setting",
      "entity": "Optimization termination and feasibility tolerances",
      "issue": "missing",
      "description": "Sec. 3 mentions convergence or a predefined iteration limit but supplies no convergence test, tolerances, monitoring window, or iteration cap.",
      "readings": [
        "Stop after relative compliance change stays below 1e-3 for 10 iterations and positive constraint violation is below 1e-4, with a 500-iteration cap.",
        "Stop after relative compliance change stays below 1e-5 for 20 iterations and positive constraint violation is below 1e-6, with a 2000-iteration cap.",
        "Run a fixed 1000 iterations."
      ],
      "effect": "layout"
    },
    {
      "category": "mesh",
      "entity": "Structured-grid resolution and replacement of adaptive meshing",
      "issue": "vague",
      "description": "Sec. 3 uses adaptive mmg refinement, while Sec. 4.1 gives only minimum and maximum element sizes. Neither the actual mesh sequence nor a unique equivalent structured grid is supplied.",
      "readings": [
        "Use a fixed uniform grid with spacing 0.01 m.",
        "Use a fixed uniform grid with spacing 0.005 m.",
        "Use a fixed uniform grid with spacing 0.0005 m."
      ],
      "effect": "layout"
    },
    {
      "category": "mesh",
      "entity": "Element interpolation and numerical integration",
      "issue": "missing",
      "description": "Sec. 3 defines generic shape functions and matrices but does not specify displacement and level-set element families, polynomial degrees, or quadrature. The stated Sobolev order alpha = 2 does not supply these choices.",
      "readings": [
        "Use four-node bilinear quadrilaterals for displacement and level set, with 2-by-2 Gauss integration.",
        "Use nine-node quadratic quadrilaterals for displacement and level set, with 3-by-3 Gauss integration.",
        "Use a uniformly triangulated structured grid with linear triangular interpolation and exact integration of the element matrices."
      ],
      "effect": "layout"
    },
    {
      "category": "mesh",
      "entity": "Discrete representation of support and traction segments",
      "issue": "missing",
      "description": "The text does not specify how Fig. 6a boundary segments are represented when their endpoints fall between structured-grid nodes or faces.",
      "readings": [
        "Snap segment endpoints to the nearest grid vertices and integrate traction over the snapped segment.",
        "Retain physical segment endpoints and integrate partial boundary-face coverage; fix nodes lying within the support interval.",
        "For a short load patch, lump its integrated resultant onto the nearest boundary node and round support patches outward to grid vertices."
      ],
      "effect": "layout"
    }
  ]
}
